Subject: Pilot agreement: liability cap & discount ask

Hi Aditya / Irene,

Thanks again for running the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward with a 3-month pilot of Redwood Inference for our telemedicine transcription workflow. Two asks from procurement/legal we need to surface early so we can get internal approval: 1) limit liability for the pilot to $250,000 aggregate and then move to a larger cap for production, and 2) indemnity limited to IP infringement only (no broad third-party or consequential coverage).

Also, procurement has requested a 25% pilot discount (pilot term, not recur) to offset integration costs. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a tiered cap for pilot vs production and the indemnity carveout? If possible, please share your proposed contractual language so we can expedite.

Thanks,

Date: 2026-10-07T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Legal summary: GlobalMed redlines & recommended path

I reviewed the attached redlines and the specific asks from GlobalMed. Summary below (high level):

- Liability cap: Customer requests $250k aggregate for the pilot period, then unspecified for production. Our standard production cap for customers at this tier is $1.5M. A tiered approach (pilot cap $250k, production cap $1.5M) is workable with exec approval given the pilot nature and low initial MRR.

- Indemnity: They want indemnity limited to IP only. Our standard indemnity covers third-party IP and claims arising from our gross negligence or willful misconduct (we carve out customers' own data issues). We can offer IP-only indemnity for pilot but should preserve broader indemnity for production or limit duration of IP-only carveout to pilot term.

- Warranty: Customer proposes multiple warranty statements that expand our exposure. Recommend keeping warranty narrowly limited to conformance with documentation and a 30-day cure period.

Risks: Accepting an IP-only indemnity and low cap without other mitigations increases residual risk if the pilot triggers broader usage. Suggested mitigations to pair with a lower pilot cap: (a) 90-day pilot window; (b) explicit usage/volume thresholds tied to cap increase; (c) logging & audit rights to validate usage; (d) escrow/holdback options if customer insists on higher discount.

Recommendation: Escalate to commercial exec (Marcus) for sign-off on a perimeter approval: allow tiered cap (pilot $250k / prod $1.5M), permit IP-only indemnity limited to pilot term, cap warranty to conformance language, and limit pilot discount to a maximum of 20% (finance prefers 15%). If Marcus approves, legal will produce a side-letter and a concise set of contract edits for a quick turnaround.

Attachment: redline_summary.docx (docx, 48KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Exec approval for GlobalMed pilot concessions (cap, indemnity, discount)

Marcus — quick ask on a strategic pilot for GlobalMed (potential to convert to a nationwide deployment). Key points:

- Ask from customer: $250k aggregate cap for 3-month pilot, IP-only indemnity during pilot, 25% one-time pilot discount.
- Our points: legal recommends tiered caps (pilot $250k / production $1.5M) and IP-only indemnity confined to pilot term. Finance recommends max 15% discount; sales prefers 20% to keep momentum.

Commercial impact: projected first-year ARR if converted ~ $420k; immediate ARR from pilot is limited but high expansion potential.

Mitigations proposed if we accept lower pilot cap: 90-day pilot term, usage gates to prevent unbounded production usage, a side-letter that reverts to standard indemnity on production sign-up, and a requirement for DocuSign by Friday to lock pricing.

Requesting your approval (one of the options below) so we can respond to procurement:
1) Approve as-laid-out: pilot cap $250k, IP-only indemnity for pilot, up to 20% pilot discount (legal side-letter required).
2) Approve with tighter pricing: pilot cap $250k, IP-only indemnity for pilot, up to 18% pilot discount (preferred by finance).
3) Decline concessions — return to standard terms.

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement is asking for a decision this week. I've attached the legal summary and the customer's redlines.

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Exec approval for GlobalMed pilot concessions (cap, indemnity, discount)

Irene — thanks for the concise summary and the risk mitigations. I authorize option 2 with a couple of conditions:

- Approve pilot cap $250k aggregate and IP-only indemnity limited strictly to the 3-month pilot.
- Approve pilot discount up to 18% (not to exceed). Sales may offer 18% for the pilot only; any additional concession requires my review.
- Require a side-letter that: (a) sets a 90-day pilot window, (b) defines usage thresholds that automatically convert to production pricing/cap, and (c) explicitly preserves Redwood's standard indemnity upon conversion to production.
- Legal to insert a warranty limitation: warranties limited to conformance with published API behavior and a 30-day remedy period.

Please prepare the side-letter and DocuSign envelope; Aditya, close with Priya and secure signatures by EOD Friday. Laura — once the side-letter is drafted, please route to me for a quick stamp.

Marcus Lin
VP, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: exec_approval_signed.pdf (pdf, 24KB)
